# Introduction

## What is Interior Habitat?

Due to a global decline in biodiversity, the conservation and restoration of biodiversity is a priority @UN2020. The global decline in biodiversity is predominantly due to habitat loss, climate change, invasive species, unsustainable resource harvesting, and pollution @Millennium2005. Alberta Environment and Parks developed an “Interior Habitat” indicator to measure and track habitat loss from anthropogenic disturbance and habitat gain from recovery of temporary disturbance in the province. Anthropogenic disturbance typically replaces habitat with ‘human footprints’ for the purposes of settlement, agriculture, resource extraction and transportation. Replacing habitat with human footprints has been shown to harm biodiversity [@Vitousek1997; @Crooks1999; @Laurence2002; @Sanderson2002]. The Interior Habitat indicator attempts to quantify one facet of biodiversity loss by capturing both the direct loss of habitat, and the additional impact of edge effects.

The Interior Habitat indicator is designed to capture edge effects around human footprints @Franklin1991. An “edge” is the boundary, or interface, between two biological communities or between different landscape elements @BCMF1998. In this context, an edge effect due to human footprints occurs when the impact of human footprints extend beyond the footprint boundaries, influencing the ability of the surrounding area to provide suitable habitat [@Lovejoy1986; @Gascon2000; @Laurence2002]. Anthropogenic edge effects alter habitat in many ways. Microclimatic conditions are altered in edges through increased penetration of sunlight and wind @Didham1999, along with increases in temperature @Cadnasso1997 and decreases in air and soil moisture [@Franklin1991; @Williams1998]. Changes in microclimate, vegetation, predation, brood parasitism and competition along forest edges have resulted in population declines of species that depend on forest interior conditions [@Strelke1980; @Wilcove1985; @Noss1990; @Robbins1989]. Species will also avoid human footprints due to pollutants, pesticides, toxicants, invasive species, traffic, and noise [@Dyer2001; @Gelbard2003; @Desserud2010; @Sliwinski2012]. All these impacts fragment habitat and decrease biodiversity [@Murcia1995; @BCMF1998; @Davis2004; @Harper2005; @Harper2007].
